transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Ever since that car drove into the crowd, even little sounds make me feel like I’m back there and I jump out of my chair or drop things. I'm just so shaken up, Doctor.
Do you experience any recurring, distressing memories or flashbacks of the car driving into the crowd, and if so, how often do they occur?

Yes, all week it's been like a film stuck on repeat in my mind, happening out of nowhere while I'm just washing dishes or trying to read the paper. I keep seeing that car jump the curb, my friend's body flying, and all the blood on the pavement. It feels so real that I have to grip the kitchen counter just to steady myself.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of the car accident, or are there things you used to enjoy that you've stopped doing since it happened?

Yes, I've been turning down rides past downtown and skipping Mass, the senior center, and my art classes because just thinking about crowds or busy streets makes my chest tighten. I've basically been staying inside my apartment and even put off getting groceries because I feel too on edge to leave.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're in a safe environment, like your apartment?

I'm not really sure if I'm actively looking out for danger, to be honest. But I do know that I am incredibly jumpy, and even the smallest sudden noise inside my own apartment makes me startle and shakes me to my core.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'incredibly jumpy' and if you've noticed any difficulty falling or staying asleep since the accident?

By jumpy, I mean that even a cabinet door closing hard or a motorcycle outside makes me jump out of my chair like a bomb went off, leaving my heart pounding for minutes. As for sleep, I lie awake staring at the ceiling for hours, and when I finally nod off, I jerk awake repeatedly with my heart racing and those awful street fair images in my head.
Do you feel like you're always waiting for something bad to happen, even when everything seems calm and safe around you?

Yes, that's exactly it. I feel like I can never let my guard down, even when I'm inside my own apartment where I should be safe. I'm constantly on edge, jumping out of my skin at any little noise and feeling like I'm just waiting for the next disaster to strike.
Do you often find yourself thinking about what you could have done differently during the car accident, or feeling guilty about surviving when others may have been hurt?

I haven't really thought about what I could have done differently or felt guilty in that way. I'm mostly just feeling completely overwhelmed and shaken up, and I've been having a lot of trouble remembering parts of what actually happened that day.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself, or like things around you aren't real, especially when you're having those flashbacks or memories of the accident?

No, I don't feel like I'm outside of my body or that things aren't real. It is actually the opposite—those memories and flashbacks feel all too real, and they completely overwhelm me when they happen.

You mentioned that the memories and flashbacks feel very real, but can you tell me if you've experienced any feelings of detachment from yourself or the world around you at any other times, not just during the flashbacks?

No, I haven't really experienced any feelings of detachment like that from myself or the world. My main struggles are just feeling constantly on edge, jumping out of my skin at every little noise, and being too afraid to leave my apartment.
Have you felt numb or disconnected from your emotions or physical sensations at any point since the accident, outside of the flashbacks or memories of the event?

No, I haven't really felt numb or disconnected from my emotions or my body. It is actually the exact opposite—I feel constantly on edge, incredibly jumpy, and completely overwhelmed by anxiety ever since the accident.
